newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end with pared gains, feeder mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end with pared gains, feeder mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures pared the advance late but held gains on continued expectations for a bottoming in the cash beef market, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.075 to 0.350 cent higher, with April up 0.200 at 67.175 cents a lb. Feeders finished 0.150 cent higher to 0.100 lower, with May off 0.075 at 69.875 cents.

Cash beef is near a bottom and demand for beef is seen rising in the grilling season. Although boxed beef prices were mostly lower again at noon and at lowest levels since late Febraury, increased sales point to the bottoming action, traders said.

Lighter-than-expected fund selling early in June also prompted shortcovering. Some traders said charts look negative and expected fund selling while others noted that weekly charts still show a trading range and there is no reason to expect active fund liquiation. This prompted ideas that June may be oversold, they said.
Active fed cattle trade early in the week also prompted talk that packers are short bought. This could add to strength in live markets is beef prices start to turn higher, they added.

RBH continued to sell April but buying by R.J. O'Brien, an early seller, and LFG lifted prices. R.J. O'Brien bought June while Prudential Securities and LFG sold. Rosenthal Collins spread long October/short June while Lind-Waldock spread long June/short October, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, R.J. O'Brien sold August 62 puts early with commercials and locals on the other side. Commission houses sold June 60 puts and bought June 64 calls, pit sources added.
Feeder futures pared early losses following the break in corn futures late, traders said.

Feeders had been under pressure early from the higher corn futures and profit taking following recent gains. Some tradres also said the market looked like it was topping technically which offset another rise in the latest CME feeder cattle index early, traders said.
Analysts expected cash feeders to remain strong from both feedlot replacement and demand for light-weight cattle to go on the improved southwest grazing areas, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.41 at $71.22 per cwt, the highest level since February 24, 1995.

R.J. O'Brien sold late while Stone Traders bought May against short October live cattle. Cargill Investor Services was on both sides of the November feeder cattle/April live cattle spread early and spread long August futures/short February live cattle, pit sources said.
